title: Day 78 · Week 11, Day 1 — Brain: touch, the first sense — the mouth at seven and a half weeks, the palms this week, reflexes that bypass the brain, the waiting room under the cortex, and the father's chest
summary: Touch is the first sense to work. Humphrey's Pittsburgh films (Prog Brain Res 1964) traced the order: a hair stroked around the mouth draws a whole-body turn at about 7.5 weeks (~Day 52), the palms respond with a partial grasp at ~10.5–11 weeks (this week), the soles at ~12 and most of the body by ~14 — reflex arcs through the spinal cord and brainstem, not experience. The thalamic fibres that carry touch to the cortex wait for weeks in the transient subplate (Kostović & Judaš, 500+ brains) and connect in the late second and third trimester; the JAMA systematic review (Lee 2005) puts conscious pain perception unlikely before the third trimester, with the dissent (Derbyshire & Bockmann 2020) labelled as contested. Ordinary touch tunes the developing spinal circuits (Fitzgerald 2005). Third-trimester fetuses respond to a mother's touch on the abdomen in small 4D studies (Marx & Nagy 2015, 2017). After birth, C-tactile fibres code slow, pleasant stroking at 1–10 cm/s (Löken 2009); skin-to-skin contact across 46 trials raises breastfeeding at 1–4 months (RR 1.24), and a small trial found babies on the father's chest after caesarean cried less (Erlandsson 2007).
action: Add a Birth plan section to the pregnancy file with one line: "If she can't do skin-to-skin straight away, I do it. Ask the hospital: can the father do skin-to-skin in theatre or recovery after a caesarean?"
